title.it: I tempi del racconto: had been walking
title.en: I had been walking for hours

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj se je dogajalo do nekega trenutka (I had been walking for hours), zakaj je bilo nekaj tako, in v pripovedi izbereš pravi pretekli čas.
goal.de: Du sagst, was bis zu einem Moment im Gang war (I had been walking for hours) und warum etwas so war, und wählst beim Erzählen die richtige Vergangenheit.
goal.it: Dici che cosa era in corso fino a un momento (I had been walking for hours) e perché una cosa era così, e nel racconto scegli il passato giusto.
goal.en: You can say what had been going on up to a moment (I had been walking for hours) and why something was so, and choose the right past tense in a story.

say.sl: **had been** + -ing pove, kaj se je dogajalo do nekega trenutka v preteklosti. **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** (Hodil{m:|f:a} sem že več ur, ko sem {m:zagledal|f:zagledala} gostilno.) Oblika je za vse osebe ista: **She had been waiting since nine when the bus came.** (Čakala je že od devetih, ko je prišel avtobus.) Slovenščina reče preteklik in *že*.
say.de: **had been** + -ing sagt, was bis zu einem Moment in der Vergangenheit schon im Gang war. **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** (Ich war schon seit Stunden unterwegs, als ich das Gasthaus sah.) Für alle Personen gleich: **She had been waiting since nine when the bus came.** (Sie wartete seit neun, als der Bus kam.) Deutsch sagt Vergangenheit und *seit*.
say.it: **had been** + -ing dice che cosa era in corso fino a un momento del passato. **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** (Camminavo da ore quando ho visto la locanda.) È uguale per tutte le persone: **She had been waiting since nine when the bus came.** (Aspettava dalle nove quando è arrivato l'autobus.) L'italiano dice l'imperfetto e *da*.
say.en: **had been** + -ing says what had been going on up to a moment in the past. **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** The same for every person: **She had been waiting since nine when the bus came.**

examples.en: I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.
examples.sl: Hodil{m:|f:a} sem že več ur, ko sem {m:zagledal|f:zagledala} gostilno.
examples.de: Ich war schon seit Stunden unterwegs, als ich das Gasthaus sah.
examples.it: Camminavo da ore quando ho visto la locanda.

examples.en: She had been waiting since nine when the bus came.
examples.sl: Čakala je že od devetih, ko je prišel avtobus.
examples.de: Sie wartete seit neun, als der Bus kam.
examples.it: Aspettava dalle nove quando è arrivato l'autobus.

say.sl: Kratko **'d been**, zanikano **hadn't been**, v vprašanju **had** spredaj: **How long had you been waiting?** (Kako dolgo si že {m:čakal|f:čakala}?) **We hadn't been walking long when it started to snow.** (Nismo še dolgo hodili, ko je začelo snežiti.) **She'd been crying.** (Jokala je.)
say.de: Kurz **'d been**, verneint **hadn't been**, in der Frage **had** vorn: **How long had you been waiting?** (Wie lange hattest du schon gewartet?) **We hadn't been walking long when it started to snow.** (Wir waren noch nicht lange unterwegs, als es zu schneien begann.) **She'd been crying.** (Sie hatte geweint.)
say.it: Breve **'d been**, al negativo **hadn't been**, nella domanda **had** davanti: **How long had you been waiting?** (Da quanto aspettavi?) **We hadn't been walking long when it started to snow.** (Non camminavamo da molto quando ha cominciato a nevicare.) **She'd been crying.** (Aveva pianto.)
say.en: Short **'d been**, with not **hadn't been**, and to ask, **had** comes first: **How long had you been waiting?** **We hadn't been walking long when it started to snow.** **She'd been crying.**

say.sl: **had been** + -ing pove tudi, zakaj je bilo nekaj tako, ko se je to še videlo. **His boots were wet: he had been walking in the beck.** (Škornji so mu bili mokri: hodil je po potoku.) **Her eyes were red: she had been crying.** (Oči je imela rdeče: jokala je.)
say.de: **had been** + -ing sagt auch, warum etwas so war, wenn man es noch sah. **His boots were wet: he had been walking in the beck.** (Seine Stiefel waren nass: Er war im Bach gegangen.) **Her eyes were red: she had been crying.** (Ihre Augen waren rot: Sie hatte geweint.)
say.it: **had been** + -ing dice anche perché una cosa era così, quando si vedeva ancora. **His boots were wet: he had been walking in the beck.** (Aveva gli stivali bagnati: aveva camminato nel torrente.) **Her eyes were red: she had been crying.** (Aveva gli occhi rossi: aveva pianto.)
say.en: **had been** + -ing also says why something was so, when you could still see it. **His boots were wet: he had been walking in the beck.** **Her eyes were red: she had been crying.**

say.sl: **had been** + -ing pove, kako dolgo, **had** + deležnik pa koliko: **She had been baking all morning.** (Pekla je vse dopoldne.) **She had baked forty scones.** (Spekla je štirideset sconesov.) Pri **know**, **own**, **be** in podobnih ni -ing: **I had known him for years.** (Poznal{m:|f:a} sem ga že leta.)
say.de: **had been** + -ing sagt, wie lange, **had** + Partizip, wie viele: **She had been baking all morning.** (Sie hatte den ganzen Vormittag gebacken.) **She had baked forty scones.** (Sie hatte vierzig Scones gebacken.) Bei **know**, **own**, **be** und ähnlichen kein -ing: **I had known him for years.** (Ich kannte ihn schon seit Jahren.)
say.it: **had been** + -ing dice quanto tempo, **had** + participio quanti: **She had been baking all morning.** (Aveva infornato tutta la mattina.) **She had baked forty scones.** (Aveva sfornato quaranta scone.) Con **know**, **own**, **be** e simili niente -ing: **I had known him for years.** (Lo conoscevo da anni.)
say.en: **had been** + -ing says how long, **had** + the participle how many: **She had been baking all morning.** **She had baked forty scones.** With **know**, **own**, **be** and the like, no -ing: **I had known him for years.**

examples.de: Sie hatte den ganzen Vormittag gebacken.

say.sl: Štirje pretekli časi v pripovedi: **The door opened.** (kaj se je zgodilo potem) **It was raining.** (kaj se je ravno dogajalo) **He had lost his way.** (kaj je bilo pred tem) **He had been walking for hours.** (kaj se je dogajalo pred tem)
say.de: Vier Vergangenheiten in einer Geschichte: **The door opened.** (was dann geschah) **It was raining.** (was gerade los war) **He had lost his way.** (was vorher war) **He had been walking for hours.** (was vorher schon im Gang war)
say.it: Quattro passati in un racconto: **The door opened.** (che cosa è successo dopo) **It was raining.** (che cosa stava succedendo) **He had lost his way.** (che cosa era successo prima) **He had been walking for hours.** (che cosa era in corso prima)
say.en: Four past tenses in a story: **The door opened.** (what happened next) **It was raining.** (what was going on) **He had lost his way.** (what came before) **He had been walking for hours.** (what had been going on before)

say.sl: **was walking** je to, kar se je ravno dogajalo, **had been walking** pa, kako dolgo že: **I was walking home when I saw him.** **I had been walking for hours when I saw him.** V govoru ljudje rečejo tudi **was sat**, **was stood**: *I was sat by the fire*. Pisno velja **was sitting**, **was standing**. Zgodbo povedo tudi v sedanjiku: *So I'm walking up the fell and this man comes up to me.*
say.de: **was walking** ist, was gerade los war, **had been walking**, wie lange schon: **I was walking home when I saw him.** **I had been walking for hours when I saw him.** Gesprochen sagt man auch **was sat**, **was stood**: *I was sat by the fire*. Geschrieben gilt **was sitting**, **was standing**. Man erzählt auch im Präsens: *So I'm walking up the fell and this man comes up to me.*
say.it: **was walking** è ciò che stava succedendo, **had been walking** da quanto tempo: **I was walking home when I saw him.** **I had been walking for hours when I saw him.** A voce si dice anche **was sat**, **was stood**: *I was sat by the fire*. Per iscritto vale **was sitting**, **was standing**. Si racconta anche al presente: *So I'm walking up the fell and this man comes up to me.*
say.en: **was walking** is what was going on, **had been walking** how long already: **I was walking home when I saw him.** **I had been walking for hours when I saw him.** In talk people also say **was sat**, **was stood**: *I was sat by the fire*. Writing wants **was sitting**, **was standing**. People also tell a story in the present: *So I'm walking up the fell and this man comes up to me.*

title.en: A wet night at the Packhorse

exercises.title: Mrs Birkett's story
exercises.text: It ___ (be) a wet night in November. It ___ (rain) since the morning. I ___ (sit) by the fire when someone knocked. I opened the door, and there ___ (stand) a man with no coat. He ___ (walk) for hours, he said. He ___ (lose) his map on the fell. His boots were full of water: he ___ (cross) the beck. I ___ (give) him some soup.

translation.sl: Bila je mokra novembrska noč. Deževalo je že od jutra. Sedela sem ob ognju, ko je nekdo potrkal. Odprla sem vrata in tam je stal moški brez plašča. Hodil je že več ur, je rekel. Na hribu je izgubil zemljevid. Škornje je imel polne vode: prečkal je potok. Dala sem mu juhe.
translation.de: Es war eine nasse Novembernacht. Es regnete schon seit dem Morgen. Ich saß beim Feuer, als jemand klopfte. Ich machte die Tür auf, und da stand ein Mann ohne Mantel. Er war schon seit Stunden unterwegs, sagte er. Er hatte am Berg seine Karte verloren. Seine Stiefel waren voller Wasser: Er hatte den Bach durchquert. Ich gab ihm Suppe.
translation.it: Era una notte bagnata di novembre. Pioveva dalla mattina. Ero seduta accanto al fuoco quando qualcuno ha bussato. Ho aperto la porta, e lì c'era un uomo senza cappotto. Camminava da ore, ha detto. Aveva perso la cartina sul monte. Aveva gli stivali pieni d'acqua: aveva attraversato il torrente. Gli ho dato della minestra.
translation.en: It was a wet night in November. It had been raining since the morning. I was sitting by the fire when someone knocked. I opened the door, and there was a man standing there with no coat. He had been walking for hours, he said. He had lost his map on the fell. His boots were full of water: he had crossed the beck. I gave him some soup.

exercises.title: Old Wilf's story
exercises.text: By 1990 I ___ (work) at the mill for forty years. One morning I ___ (walk) to work when I saw smoke. The fire ___ (burn) all night. Someone ___ (leave) a lamp on. We ___ (run) to the beck for water.

translation.sl: Leta 1990 sem delal v mlinu že štirideset let. Nekega jutra sem šel na delo, ko sem zagledal dim. Ogenj je gorel vso noč. Nekdo je pustil prižgano svetilko. Stekli smo po vodo k potoku.
translation.de: 1990 arbeitete ich schon seit vierzig Jahren in der Mühle. Eines Morgens war ich auf dem Weg zur Arbeit, als ich Rauch sah. Das Feuer hatte die ganze Nacht gebrannt. Jemand hatte eine Lampe brennen lassen. Wir rannten zum Bach um Wasser.
translation.it: Nel 1990 lavoravo al mulino da quarant'anni. Una mattina stavo andando al lavoro quando ho visto del fumo. Il fuoco aveva bruciato tutta la notte. Qualcuno aveva lasciato una lampada accesa. Siamo corsi al torrente a prendere l'acqua.
translation.en: By 1990 I had been working at the mill for forty years. One morning I was walking to work when I saw smoke. The fire had been burning all night. Someone had left a lamp on. We ran to the beck for water.
